question: What is the primary purpose of an assisted living facility?

options.A: Acting as a permanent psychiatric hospital alternative
options.B: Offering temporary shelter for acute surgical recovery
options.D: Bridging the gap between independent living and nursing homes

explanation: Assisted living facilities are specifically designed for individuals who need some help with daily tasks but do not require intensive, round-the-clock nursing care. [learn more](GNS324_U5_T6#GNS324_U5_T6_h1)

question: A key philosophical focus of modern assisted living care is...

options.A: Encouraging resident independence and personal choice
options.B: Removing all physical activity to prevent any falls
options.C: Restricting family visits to maintain facility security

explanation: Modern assisted living prioritizes resident dignity, autonomy, and personal choice while providing necessary support services. [learn more](GNS324_U5_T6#GNS324_U5_T6_h1)

question: What assessment is primarily conducted before admitting a new resident?

options.A: A complete surgical clearance by a specialist surgeon
options.B: A comprehensive evaluation of physical and cognitive needs
options.C: A mandatory full psychiatric commitment hearing
options.D: A financial audit of family savings accounts

explanation: Pre-admission assessments ensure the facility has the appropriate resources and staff capabilities to care for the incoming resident safely. [learn more](GNS324_U5_T6#GNS324_U5_T6_h2)

question: Why might an applicant with unstable medical needs be denied admission to an assisted living facility?

options.A: Insurance companies never cover medical equipment in these centers
options.B: Other residents prefer living only with completely healthy peers
options.C: Assisted living only accepts residents who are completely independent
options.D: Such conditions require continuous skilled nursing care beyond facility scope

explanation: Assisted living facilities are not equipped to provide the 24-hour skilled medical supervision required for unstable health conditions. [learn more](GNS324_U5_T6#GNS324_U5_T6_h2)

question: What is an example of an Activity of Daily Living (ADL)?
explanation: ADLs refer to fundamental self-care tasks essential for daily living, including bathing, dressing, eating, and toileting. [learn more](GNS324_U5_T6#GNS324_U5_T6_h3)

question: A resident can wash their upper body but needs help tying shoes and buttoning shirts. What nursing approach is best?

options.A: Force the resident to complete everything without any help
options.B: Report the resident for failing to dress independently
options.C: Assist only with the specific tasks the resident cannot manage
options.D: Take over all dressing tasks completely to save time

explanation: Caregivers should encourage remaining functional abilities by only assisting with tasks the resident cannot safely perform alone. [learn more](GNS324_U5_T6#GNS324_U5_T6_h3)

question: What is a primary responsibility of a nurse working in an assisted living facility?

options.A: Coordinating healthcare services and supervising caregiving staff
options.B: Ordering groceries and planning facility menus
options.C: Performing major surgical procedures on-site daily
options.D: Managing the financial investments of the facility

explanation: Assisted living nurses focus on health monitoring, care coordination, staff supervision, and liaising with external medical providers. [learn more](GNS324_U5_T6#GNS324_U5_T6_h4)

question: How does the role of an assisted living nurse differ from a traditional hospital nurse?

options.A: Assisted living nurses do not require any formal nursing qualification
options.B: Hospital nurses never interact with doctors, unlike assisted living nurses
options.C: Hospital nurses provide acute bedside care, while assisted living nurses focus on chronic care coordination
options.D: Assisted living nurses perform surgeries while hospital nurses only clean rooms

explanation: Assisted living nursing emphasizes wellness, chronic disease monitoring, and supervisory roles rather than acute hospital care. [learn more](GNS324_U5_T6#GNS324_U5_T6_h4)

question: Why is medication management considered a high-risk activity in assisted living?

options.A: Pharmacies refuse to deliver drugs to residential facilities
options.B: Residents often receive multiple prescriptions from various doctors
options.C: Nurses are not allowed to touch any prescription bottles
options.D: Medications are extremely expensive to purchase

explanation: Managing multiple medications from different prescribers increases the risk of drug interactions, dosing errors, and adverse reactions. [learn more](GNS324_U5_T6#GNS324_U5_T6_h5)

question: What is an essential safety protocol regarding medication storage in these facilities?

options.A: Storing all clinical supplies in the facility kitchen
options.B: Keeping all drugs unlocked on dining tables for easy access
options.C: Storing medications securely and maintaining accurate administration records
options.D: Allowing residents to share their painkillers freely

explanation: Secure storage and precise documentation prevent accidental ingestion, theft, and medication administration errors. [learn more](GNS324_U5_T6#GNS324_U5_T6_h5)

question: What is a negative consequence of excessive overprotection by facility staff?

options.A: Improved physical strength and faster walking speeds
options.B: Increased interest in complex community activities
options.C: Better compliance with medication administration schedules
options.D: Rapid physical and psychological decline in the resident

explanation: Removing all autonomy and risk can cause residents to lose their remaining physical abilities and experience depression. [learn more](GNS324_U5_T6#GNS324_U5_T6_h6)

question: Which strategy best promotes quality of life for assisted living residents?

options.A: Forcing all residents to follow an identical daily routine
options.B: Encouraging social engagement and participation in tailored activities
options.C: Discouraging family visits to maintain strict facility quiet
options.D: Confining residents to their rooms to prevent accidental falls

explanation: Socialization, mental stimulation, and recreational opportunities are vital components of emotional and physical well-being. [learn more](GNS324_U5_T6#GNS324_U5_T6_h6)

question: What is the primary purpose of facility inspections in assisted living?

options.A: To test the cooking skills of the facility chefs
options.B: To reduce the monthly salary expenses of the facility
options.C: To market vacant rooms to prospective new clients
options.D: To ensure compliance with safety, health, and legal standards

explanation: Routine inspections protect residents by verifying that the facility meets all mandatory health, safety, and operational regulations. [learn more](GNS324_U5_T6#GNS324_U5_T6_h7)

question: Which of the following is NOT typically covered by assisted living regulatory standards?
explanation: Regulations focus on resident care, safety, staffing, and facility operations, not the private financial investments of the corporate owners. [learn more](GNS324_U5_T6#GNS324_U5_T6_h7)
